import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set the style of the visualization
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a barplot to compare average price by brand
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
avg_price_by_brand = df.groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)
sns.barplot(x=avg_price_by_brand.index, y=avg_price_by_brand.values, palette='viridis')
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.xlabel('Brand')
plt.ylabel('Average Price (USD)')
plt.title('Average Camera Price by Brand')
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Set the style of the visualization
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create a barplot to compare average price by brand
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))
avg_price_by_brand = df.groupby('brand')['price_usd'].mean().sort_values(ascending=False)
sns.barplot(x=avg_price_by_brand.index, y=avg_price_by_brand.values, palette='viridis')
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')
plt.xlabel('Brand')
plt.ylabel('Average Price (USD)')
plt.title('Average Camera Price by Brand')
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
